title: Non-Go projects: ork projects setup for the check command and shell allowlist, and a warning when they are missing
lead: *Proposed.* The owner sets up a non-Go project for ork in one command: `ork projects set NAME --check CMD --preset python` stores the check command and a full implementer allowlist for that language. `--allow ROLE=PATTERN` adds a pattern to the role's list instead of replacing it, and `--replace-allow` replaces it. `ork run`, the TUI launch confirm and `ork doctor` warn when a project has no check command, when a project without `go.mod` gets the built-in Go allowlist, and when an allowlist lacks Edit, Write or a pattern for the check command. The command shape, the preset contents, the warning texts and the busy rule are open: see `Open owner questions`. Ask the owner before the relay starts; the names below (`--preset`, `--replace-allow`, `allow_add`, `implementer_preset`, `warnings`) are part of the questions.
findings_note: 2026-11-03: the slicer project had no check_command and no implementer permissions in the ork registry, so its Claude implementers were denied python3 (the default allowlist is Go-centric, internal/engine/perm.go:24-36), and the project check step had nothing to run, so a slice could pass with no tests. Found only from a screenshot of denied commands. Friction: (1) ork doctor and the launch plan do not warn when a project has no check command. (2) 'ork projects set --allow ROLE=PATTERN' replaces the role's whole list with the patterns given in that call: one call with a single pattern left an implementer that could not Read or Edit, and a second call dropped the first pattern; the plan printed only 'allowlist: Bash(python3 -m unittest*)' with no warning. (3) 'ork projects set' is refused while the project has unfinished runs, so a launched wave must be stopped before its project can be fixed. Proposed: a setup step or preset per language (go, python) that sets the check command and a full allowlist; --allow adds to the list unless told to replace; a warning in doctor and in the plan. Owner decision on the presets. Related: S243, S249, S251, S258.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** reading slicer's check_command key (S246); S249's setup steps (slicer init, matrix init, adj); a TUI settings editor (S251); presets other than go and python; removing one pattern from a list; storing a run's project settings in its run record (Q5 option d); any change to the Codex sandbox or to the Claude brief (S243).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
2026-11-03 (the findings of this item): the slicer project (Python; its suite is `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, `slicer/AGENTS.md:23`) had no `check_command` and no implementer permissions in ork's registry. Its Claude implementers were denied `python3`, and the project check had nothing to run, so a slice could pass with no tests. This was found only from a screenshot of denied commands. Then `ork projects set --allow implementer=PATTERN` left the implementer with only that pattern (no Read, no Edit), a second call dropped the first pattern, the launch plan printed only `allowlist: Bash(python3 -m unittest*)` with no warning, and `ork projects set` was refused while the project had unfinished runs.

What the code at HEAD of main shows (read 2026-11-03):

- The built-in implementer allowlist is Go-centric. `DefaultImplementerAllowlist` (`internal/engine/perm.go:24-36`) holds Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, `Bash(slicer *)`, read-only git and `git -C` forms, `Bash(go -C * test*)`, `Bash(go -C * vet*)`, `Bash(go test*)`, `Bash(go vet*)`, `Bash(gofmt *)`, four read-only adj forms, and `Bash(<check command>*)` when a check command is set (adj 75 `launch.default-allowlist`, adj 94 `engine.default-allowlist`). So setting only `--check "python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests"` would already have allowed that one command for a project with no registry entry, but not `python3 -m unittest tests.test_x`, `TMPDIR=... python3 -m unittest ...` or `python3 tests/affected.py --run`, which `slicer/AGENTS.md:36` and `:41` tell agents to use.
- A registry list replaces the default as a whole (`ResolvePermission`, `perm.go:58-68`; `TestImplementerGetsTheRegistryAllowlistAsIs`, `internal/engine/perm_test.go:36`). Only Claude is held to it: Codex has no per-tool allowlist and runs `workspace-write` (`docs/design.md:984-986`, adj 100), so the denials hit only Claude implementers, including the Claude fallback of S243.
- `--allow` replaces by design. The CLI collects the patterns of one call per role (`setPermissionsAndVendorEnv`, `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:491-504`) and the daemon sets the role's entry to that list (`withProjectExtras`, `internal/daemon/settings.go:63-79`). This was the owner's decision for S174 on 2026-10-29 ("permissions and vendor env change per role and per key", S174 note), and the usage text and guide say so (`internal/cli/cli.go:102-103`; `docs/guide.md:149`; `docs/state.md:132-133`). `TestProjectsSetEnvLinePermissionAndAllowFlags` (`internal/cli/cli_test.go:1476`) pins it. Nothing checks that a list still holds Read, Edit or Write.
- With no check command the engine runs only `slicer check` (`internal/engine/states.go:207-236`) and the brief says so (`internal/engine/brief.go:107-111`). The plan prints `check: ` with nothing after it (`internal/cli/run.go:180`; TUI `internal/tui/launch.go:498`), and the allowlist line prints the list as it is (`run.go:195-201`, `launch.go:514-519`). The plan has one free-text `note` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:87`), used for a failed matrix read and an out vendor, shown under the plan rows (`run.go:204-206`, `launch.go:521-525`, in the Warn style).
- `ork doctor` (S71, done) checks for each project: the path exists and is a directory; a configured check command passes `sh -n -c` and its first word resolves on PATH or in the project; nonempty worktree and branch patterns hold `{id}` or `{id_lower}` (`internal/cli/doctor.go:173-221`; `docs/design.md:1524-1534`). It never runs the command. It does not look at a missing check command (pinned as no finding by `TestDoctorProjectWithoutCheckCommandIsNotAnError`, `internal/cli/cli_test.go:791`) or at permissions at all. Project findings print `[WARN]` and keep exit 0 (`doctor.go:516-525`; `TestDoctorProjectFindingsKeepExitZero`, `cli_test.go:799`).
- The busy refusal was the owner's decision for S161 on 2026-10-27 ("refuses while the project has unfinished runs", S161 note). `setProject` refuses any field with `project_busy` (`internal/daemon/handlers.go:585-593`). The reason holds for most fields: a run's engine keeps a copy of the project from its start (`internal/daemon/runs.go:576-577`) and reads `CheckCommand`, `CheckMinutes`, permissions, environment lines, `UIDoc`, `UIPassSkills` and `Push` from it each round (`internal/engine/round.go:217`, `:263-267`; `states.go:198-233`; `internal/engine/land.go:86`), but a daemon restart reloads every unfinished run with the registry as it is then (`runs.go:236-260`), so a change would reach a running slice at an unknown point. Some fields are never read by a started run: the cap is read at each admission from the registry (`hasRoomLocked`, `runs.go:801-821`), the budgets are copied into the run record at start (`internal/engine/engine.go:276-280`; read from `rec.Budgets` at `round.go:150-162`), and the worktree and branch patterns are used only when a run is planned and created (`engine.go:140-160`). A set between a plan and its start is already refused at admission with "plan changed" (`runs.go:563-568`).
- `adj 32` (`project.check-command`) says ork prefers slicer's `check_command` key once it exists; slicer has it (s379, done) and S246 (v1.2, open) applies it. Both slicer's and ork's own value are empty today (`slicer config check_command --root ../slicer` and `--root .` print nothing, 2026-11-03). This slice keeps reading the registry; S246 later makes the warnings use the effective command.

Related items, not changed here: S243 (the Claude implementer's brief lists its allowlist), S249 (`ork projects setup NAME STEP` for slicer init, matrix init and adj, v1.2), S251 (settings pane, v1.2), S248 (`projects set --dry-run`, v1.2, edits the same `setProject`), S258 (spec check row setting), S174 and S161 (the setter). slicer provides nothing like this: `slicer --root ../slicer find` for "allowlist", "preset" and "check command" finds only slicer's own git allowlist and s379.

Not verified: the slicer project's current registry entry and the exact denied commands (the registry and the run logs are outside the workspace and were not read); the facts above about them are from the item's findings.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Each test is written for the recommended answer of the question it names; change it with the owner's answer before the relay starts.

Engine (`internal/engine`):

- `TestImplementerPresetGoIsTheBuiltInDefault` (Q1): `ImplementerPreset("go", "go test ./...")` equals `DefaultImplementerAllowlist("go test ./...")`, and the same with `""`.
- `TestImplementerPresetPython` (Q1): `ImplementerPreset("python", "python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests")` returns exactly `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Bash(slicer *)`, `Bash(git status*)`, `Bash(git diff*)`, `Bash(git log*)`, `Bash(git -C * status*)`, `Bash(git -C * diff*)`, `Bash(git -C * log*)`, `Bash(adj check*)`, `Bash(adj lint*)`, `Bash(adj show*)`, `Bash(adj inbox*)`, `Bash(python3 -m unittest*)`, `Bash(python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests*)`, in that order. Each call returns its own slice.
- `TestImplementerPresetUnknownName` (Q1): `ImplementerPreset("rust", "")` returns the error `unknown preset "rust" (presets: go, python)`.
- `TestSetupWarnings` (Q3, Q4), a table over `SetupWarnings(p, has)` where `has` reports the files given. Name `slicer`, path `/p/slicer`:
  - Go project (`go.mod`), check `go test ./...`, no permissions: `nil`.
  - no check command, `go.mod`: `["no check command: only slicer check runs after each round (fix: ork projects set slicer --check CMD)"]`.
  - no check command, no permissions, `pyproject.toml`, no `go.mod`: the line above, then `"the implementer has the built-in Go allowlist, but slicer has no go.mod (fix: ork projects set slicer --preset python)"`.
  - no permissions, no marker file: the second line ends `(fix: ork projects set slicer --preset LANG, or --allow implementer=PATTERN)`.
  - implementer `["Bash(python3 -m unittest*)"]`, check `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`: `["the implementer allowlist has no Read, Edit, Write; it replaces the built-in list as a whole (fix: ork projects set slicer --preset python)"]` (no `go.mod` line: the project has its own list).
  - implementer `["Read", "Edit", "Write"]`, check `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`: `["the implementer allowlist has no pattern for the check command \"python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests\" (fix: ork projects set slicer --allow 'implementer=Bash(python3 -m unittest*)')"]`. A pattern matches when it is `Bash(X*)` and the command starts with X, or `Bash(X)` and the command is X.
  - implementer preset `read-only`: no allowlist line.
  - a name with a space, `my proj`: the fix reads `ork projects set 'my proj' ...` (`ShellWord`).

Daemon (`internal/daemon`):

- `TestRunPlanCarriesSetupWarnings` (Q3): a project in a temp dir with no `go.mod` and no check command: `run.plan` returns `warnings` with the two lines of the table above, in order; a temp dir with `go.mod` and `go test ./...` returns no `warnings` key in the JSON.
- `TestRunStartAcceptsAPlanWithWarnings` (Q3): `run.start` with `expected` set to that plan starts the run (no "plan changed").
- `TestProjectsSetAllowAddAppendsToTheList` (Q2): implementer `["Read","Edit"]`; `{"name":"p","allow_add":{"implementer":["Bash(python3 *)"]}}` saves `["Read","Edit","Bash(python3 *)"]`; the same call again saves the same list (no duplicate). A project with no entry and check `go test ./...` saves `DefaultImplementerAllowlist("go test ./...")` plus the pattern. `allow_add` for `reviewer` is `bad_params` `role reviewer is read-only, but the registry gives it an allowlist`. `allow_add` and `permissions` naming the same role in one call is `bad_params` `permissions and allow_add both set implementer`.
- `TestProjectsSetImplementerPreset` (Q1): `{"name":"p","check_command":"python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests","implementer_preset":"python"}` saves that check command and `ImplementerPreset("python", that command)`; with `allow_add` in the same call the added patterns follow the preset; `"rust"` is `bad_params` with the preset error; `implementer_preset` with a `permissions.implementer` entry is `bad_params`.
- `TestProjectsSetSafeFieldsWhileARunIsUnfinished` (Q5): with a paused run, each of `cap`, `worktree_pattern`, `branch_pattern`, `budget_minutes` and `budget_tokens` saves. A call that sets `cap` and `push` saves nothing and is `project_busy`.
- `TestProjectsSetRefusesAnUnfinishedRun` and `TestProjectsSetNewFieldsRefuseAnUnfinishedRun` (Q5, existing): the message becomes `project p has unfinished runs: a-run; a running slice reads push, so set it after they finish or stop (cap, budgets and patterns may change now)`, with the refused field names of the call in place of `push`.

CLI (`internal/cli`):

- `TestPrintRunPlanShowsWarnings` (Q3): a plan with two warnings prints `warning: LINE` for each after the role rows and before `note:`; a plan with an empty check command prints `check: none`.
- `TestProjectsSetAllowAdds` (Q2): `--allow implementer=Edit` on a list of two prints `permissions=implementer:3 patterns`; `--replace-allow --allow implementer=Edit` saves `["Edit"]`; `--replace-allow` without `--allow` is the usage error `--replace-allow needs --allow`.
- `TestProjectsSetPresetFlag` (Q1): `--check "python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests" --preset python` prints `updated slicer: check_command="python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests", permissions=implementer:18 patterns`; `--preset python --permission implementer=read-only` is a usage error.
- `TestProjectsSetEnvLinePermissionAndAllowFlags` (existing, `cli_test.go:1476`): the singular call `--allow implementer=Edit` now adds, so the expected list is `["Read","Bash(go test*)","Edit"]` and the line says `implementer:3 patterns`; the rest is unchanged.
- `TestDoctorProjectWithoutCheckCommandHasAFinding` (Q4), replacing `TestDoctorProjectWithoutCheckCommandIsNotAnError`: a project with `go.mod` and no check command has exactly the `no check command` finding; exit 0.
- `TestDoctorWarnsOfAnAllowlistWithoutEdit` (Q3): the registry list `["Bash(python3 -m unittest*)"]` gives the `has no Read, Edit, Write` finding; text prints `[WARN] project NAME  PATH` and the line.

TUI (`internal/tui`):

- `TestLaunchConfirmShowsSetupWarnings` (Q3): a plan with one warning and an empty check command shows `check: none` and the warning, wrapped to the width in the Warn style, above the note; a plan without warnings renders as before (the goldens do not change).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Wait for the owner's answers to Q1 to Q6 and change the tests and steps to match. Record each answer the owner picks in an interactive question with `adj decide` as AGENTS.md allows (keys under Open owner questions), and update the S161 and S174 docs lines that the answers change.
2. Write the failing tests above and watch them go red.
3. Presets (Q1): in `perm.go`, build the base list (today's default without the Go entries), add the Go or Python entries, then `Bash(<check command>*)` when the command is set. `DefaultImplementerAllowlist(check)` returns `ImplementerPreset("go", check)`, so `TestDefaultImplementerAllowlistIsExactlyTheDecidedOne` stays green unchanged.
4. Warnings (Q3, Q4): write `SetupWarnings` in `internal/engine/setup.go` with the texts of the table, in this order: check command, Go default without `go.mod`, missing Read, Edit or Write, no pattern for the check command. Move `shellWord` there as `ShellWord` and update its callers in `doctor.go`.
5. Plan: add `Warnings` to `RunPlan` and fill it in `planRun` after the permissions. The `expected` comparison at `runs.go:529-535` compares the JSON, so it needs no change.
6. Plan text: in `printRunPlan` print `check: none` for an empty command and one `warning: ` line per warning before the note; in `launch.go` the same, each wrapped like the note.
7. Doctor: in `checkProject`, append each `SetupWarnings` line as a finding, with `has` reading the project path. Keep the exit code.
8. Setter (Q1, Q2): add `allow_add` and `implementer_preset` to the wire and `SetsNothing`; validate patterns with `registry.ValidatePermissionEntry`. In `withProjectExtras`, apply `permissions`, then the preset, then `allow_add`: start from the role's current list, or from `engine.ResolvePermission` of the project as saved when the role has no entry, append each pattern not already in the list, then resolve the role as today. The CLI sends `--allow` as `allow_add`, and `--replace-allow` sends it as `permissions` (today's wire). Update the usage lines and the flag help.
9. Busy rule (Q5): in `setProject`, refuse while runs are unfinished only when the call sets a field outside `cap`, `worktree_pattern`, `branch_pattern`, `budget_minutes` and `budget_tokens`, with the new message naming the refused fields. Keep the lock order and the "plan changed" check.
10. Docs: `docs/state.md`, `docs/design.md`, `docs/guide.md` at the lines in Files, each change marked *proposed*. The guide's flags table gains `--preset LANG` and `--replace-allow`, and the `--allow` row says it adds.
11. CHANGELOG, last: one entry at the bottom of `## Unreleased` that starts "Non-Go projects:" and says: `ork projects set --preset go|python` sets a full implementer allowlist; `--allow` adds a pattern and `--replace-allow` replaces the list; the run plan, the launch confirm and `ork doctor` warn of a missing check command or an allowlist that does not fit the project; `cap`, budgets and patterns can change while runs are unfinished (each *proposed*).
12. Mutation-check each new assertion (drop the `go.mod` check, the missing-Edit check, the de-duplication in `allow_add`, the busy field list, the `check: none` text) and report which test went red.
13. UI slice: UI pass (r14).

Owner decisions: 2026-11-07 (interview). Q4: refuse a wave start or run when no check command is set, unless '--allow-no-check' is given; the error names the fix. Based on the 2026-11-04 prism-ui break. Q5 is still open.

Owner decisions: 2026-11-07 (interview), all as recommended. Q1: a flag --preset go|python on ork projects set that writes the preset's plain patterns into permissions.implementer, plus the check command pattern saved in the same call; narrow python preset (python3 -m unittest*); no registry format change. Q2: --allow adds to the role's list (starting from the effective list) and --replace-allow replaces it; this reverses the S174 replace decision for --allow only and changes TestProjectsSetEnvLinePermissionAndAllowFlags. Q3: setup warnings are a plan field printed by ork run and the TUI launch confirm and also shown as ork doctor findings (exit 0 kept), always, whether or not a Claude entry is in the implementer chain. Q4 (earlier): refuse with no check command unless --allow-no-check. Q5: ork projects set while runs are unfinished allows cap, worktree_pattern, branch_pattern, budget_minutes and budget_tokens and refuses the rest, naming the refused fields. Q6: one slice, v1.1, M (effort 3). Owner-only adj records for the reversals: cli.allow-adds and launch.no-check-command.

- `go -C WORKTREE test -race -count=1 ./internal/engine ./internal/daemon ./internal/cli ./internal/tui`, and `git -C WORKTREE status --short testdata/golden` prints nothing.

sections.heading: Open owner questions
sections.body:
Open owner questions from the 2026-11-03 spec drafting. Ask the owner before the relay starts; the spec waits on these. `adj check` finds none of the keys named below (not found, 2026-11-03).

Q1 How a project is set up, and the presets (`project.allowlist-presets`).
Options: (a) a flag on the existing setter, `ork projects set NAME --preset go|python`, that writes the preset's list into `permissions.implementer` as plain patterns, with `Bash(<check command>*)` for the check command saved in the same call (no registry format change, so an older ork reads it; the owner sees and edits the exact list; a later change of the check command does not update the list, which Q3's check-command warning catches); (b) the same flag, but the registry stores the preset's name (`"implementer": "python"`) and the engine expands it at each round as it does the default (the list follows `--check` and ork's updates; the registry gains preset names beside `read-only`, `docs/state.md:81-82`, and an older ork refuses the run with "unknown permission preset"); (c) a setup step of S249's `ork projects setup NAME STEP` (`python`, `go`) (one place for setup; waits for S249, which is v1.2); (d) no preset: ork picks the default by marker file (`go.mod` gives the Go list, `pyproject.toml` the Python list) (no owner step; changes adj 75's single built-in default, and a guess can be wrong for a mixed repo). Preset contents: the base is today's default without its five Go entries; `go` adds them back (so `go` equals today's default); `python` adds `Bash(python3 -m unittest*)`. Broader Python forms (`Bash(python3 *)`, or slicer's own `TMPDIR=* python3 -m unittest*`, `python3 tests/affected.py*`, `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer*` from `slicer/AGENTS.md:36-80`) are left to `--allow`; `Bash(python3 *)` would let the implementer run any Python, which is about what `go test` already allows. Other languages (dotnet, node): none in this slice.
Recommendation: (a), with the narrow `python` preset.
Waits: `TestImplementerPreset*`, `TestProjectsSetImplementerPreset`, `TestProjectsSetPresetFlag`, Implement steps 3 and 8.

Q2 `--allow`: add or replace (`cli.allow-adds`).
Options: (a) `--allow` adds to the role's list, starting from the effective list (the built-in default when the role has no entry), skips a pattern already there, and `--replace-allow` makes the call's patterns replace the list (what the friction asked for; reverses the S174 decision of 2026-10-29 for `--allow` only, and changes `TestProjectsSetEnvLinePermissionAndAllowFlags`); (b) keep replace, and add `--add-allow ROLE=PATTERN` (no change to a decided behavior; the surprising default stays); (c) keep replace and only warn (Q3) when the result lacks Read, Edit or Write (smallest; a second call still drops the first pattern). Removing one pattern is not in any option (`--permission implementer=` resets to the default).
Recommendation: (a).
